title: Orphaned allocator slots causing Dedicated reserved-pool shortfall during burst failover
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: During a multi-tenant traffic surge on Dedicated pools, several tenants experienced sustained request throttling despite available physical GPUs. Root cause was allocator behavior during model-variant failover: allocations were marked 'in-use' but their slot bookkeeping was not returned to the burst headroom pool after an async fallback path timed out. This produced orphaned slots and gradual reserved-pool exhaustion under burst traffic patterns.
impact_details: Affected 6 enterprise tenants in us-west-2 for 22 minutes; average SLA latency spikes to 3x baseline and request throttles for burst-level routes. Logged several paid-customer escalations and an on-call paging incident. No model inference correctness regressions observed.
timeline_summary: 2026-03-10 09:12 — Surge begins; autoscaler initiates burst allocation. 2026-03-10 09:13 — Multiple fallback flows triggered due to transient kernel OOM on a new quantized variant. 2026-03-10 09:15 — Observability shows headroom drop; tenants receive 429s. 2026-03-10 09:28 — Hotfix deployed to forcibly reclaim orphaned allocations; capacity recovered by 09:34. 2026-03-10 10:00 — Customer comms sent; postmortem started.
root_cause: A race in the allocator: when a request triggered fallback to a cheaper model variant, the fallback path used an async token that could time out independently of the original reservation. The cleanup callback relied on the async path's success to release bookkeeping. If the async path timed out or was cancelled, the release codepath was skipped, leaving the logical slot marked occupied while underlying GPU memory was freed by the kernel OOM handler. Over repeated events this produced a slow leak of available headroom.
temporary_mitigation: 1) Forced reclamation job (hotfix) that scanned pool allocations and forcibly cleared entries that were stale >30s. 2) Temporarily increased burst cap and adjusted scoring to avoid routing additional burst traffic to affected pools. 3) Notified customers and applied manual customer-specific headroom overrides where appropriate.
permanent_fix_description: Patch allocator state machine to make release of bookkeeping idempotent and unconditional on fallback async success. Add strong invariants: every reservation must register a GUID checked by a background reconciler. If reservation GUID missing after N seconds, release logical slot and emit metric. Also add an explicit cancellation path that triggers release code even when async fallback times out.
tests_and_validation: Added unit tests for idempotent release, integration test that simulates async-fallback timeouts under burst traffic, and chaos test that injects kernel-level OOMs while verifying headroom invariants. Verified in staging for 48 hours under synthetic burst load without orphaned slot growth.
rollout_plan: Canary rollout to us-west-2 dedicated pools over 3 waves (5%, 25%, 100%) with automatic rollback on: any increase in stale allocation metric > 0.5/min or customer error rate above baseline + 50%. Target full rollout by 2026-03-18.
monitoring_post_deploy: Create metric allocator.reclaimed.guids and allocator.stale_slots.count; add daily reconciliation alert if stale_slots.count > 5 for > 10 minutes. 72-hour elevated monitoring window after rollout with on-call engineer assigned.
customer_comms: Initial escalation reply sent 2026-03-10 11:02 (Ava Martinez) acknowledging impact and listing mitigation steps. Follow-up on 2026-03-11 with root cause summary and timeline. Proposed SLA credit package offered to impacted tenants; customer success coordinating acceptance.
open_questions: Should default stale timeout be 30s or 60s for conservative reclaim?
Do we need a dedicated reconciliation microservice or is background worker in allocator sufficient?
